displayDescription: A procedural 3D lens mechanism explodes along its optical axis, opens a quadrant cutaway, shows a signal-to-energy light path, then reassembles.
audioDescription: Silent preview. No music, voice or sound effects.
limitations: Illustrative procedural scene: housing, lens ring, retaining rings, aperture stop and node plate are built from Three.js ExtrudeGeometry/Sphere/Cylinder primitives, not CAD or glTF parts.
Glass uses MeshPhysicalMaterial screen-space transmission; this approximates glass and is not physically accurate refraction or lens optics.
PBR reflections come from a procedural RoomEnvironment through PMREMGenerator, not a captured HDRI.

The cutaway uses two world-space clipping planes (localClippingEnabled, clipIntersection) plus explicit cut-face cap rectangles recomputed from the cut position; caps use a flat hatch texture, which stretches slightly while the section sweeps.
The light path is a set of straight TubeGeometry segments (discrete #628BF4 signal segments, then #EF9F5C after the aperture focus). It is a diagram, not simulated light transport.
Card widths come from a fixed monospace advance estimate, so a fallback font with a different advance may change the padding a little.

The bundled Three.js file (lens-scene.js) contains Math.random for object UUIDs and requestAnimationFrame for setAnimationLoop. Neither is used for rendering or timing: every frame is derived from timeline time.
